comments.text:
Lost Vikings 2. It's a puzzle platformer, type of game, with some light combat elements. This does mean you CAN die in the game. However, on the first level there are no enemies, and no hazards.

However, you can still take fall damage. Using the shield to create a platform, and jumping from the highest point on the level to the lowest, you will take damage. Do this until one of the other characters dies, then finish the level.

You will unlock special abilities, from a massively powerful attack, infinite flight, or jump for certain characters, making the rest of the game significantly easier.

comments.text: In borderlands 2 when Jack tells you to listen to him and the jump off the side of the clip killing you, I did it without hesitation and I did it because of something I found out years ago. First of all, let me just say that I’ve been playing video games since the first PlayStation was given to me by my father and ever since then I’ve been playing video games a lot. I’m hooked. Back then the only thing that we could do for a long period of time was played by ourselves and if you play it enough times you sometimes to find an Easter egg or some hidden achievement.  Eventually, I started to realize that developers would give you a achievement for doing something stupid or pretty damn messed up and if you don’t believe me, look it up for yourself I mean the prime example of this is in borderlands 2 when Jack tells you to listen to him and when he tells you to jump off the side, killing yourself. You get a nice decent reward and I think you get achievement even if you don’t get an achievement you still get a pretty good reward out of it. So when you get an achievement and you’re thinking, wow that was pretty messed up with me don’t feel so bad because it’s the developers that made the game that way that are the ones that are really messed up just something to think about.
